en: Sutta Nipāta 2.8 Dhamma (nāvā) Sutta:
For when a person understands the Dhamma,
The deities should worship him as they would Indra;
being thus honored, with a mind full of serene confidence,
he, being learned, proclaims the Dhamma.
Having applied himself to that and reflected upon it,
the wise one who practices in accordance with the Dhamma becomes discerning, insightful, and subtle.
He who, being heedful, associates with such a person—
though he may attend upon one who is petty, foolish, envious,
and intent on the future— [will not suffer].
Without having realized the Dhamma right here,
one approaches death with doubts not yet crossed over,
like a man who has descended into a river.
In the great waters of a swift-flowing torrent,
being carried away and following the current,
how could he possibly enable others to cross over?
Likewise, one who has not clarified the Dhamma for himself,
who has not mastered the meaning from those of great learning,
being ignorant and having not crossed over doubt—
How could he possibly inspire confidence in others?
He is like one who has boarded a sturdy ship but is accompanied only by a small, empty basket.
Thus, one who knows the means,
who is skillful and possessed of wisdom, may deliver many others there as well. Likewise,
he who has realized the Vedas and whose self is cultivated—
He is learned and possesses a nature free from agitation;
he can convince others who possess understanding,
provided they are attentive and ready to receive his words.
Therefore, indeed, one should associate with a true person who is wise and learned;
practicing after having understood the meaning, one will attain the goal.
"One who has understood the Dhamma will find happiness.
Thus ends the eighth discourse, the *Nāvāsutta*.
